subject: Affordability sizing & savings walkthrough — post-demo next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Clara Nguyen <clara@fiscotech.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Affordability sizing & savings walkthrough — post-demo next steps

Hi Clara —

Thanks again for taking the demo with us this morning. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed set of next steps so your team can share with procurement: 

Key pain & goals you called out
- High token spend on intent classification + summarization (peak inference ~= 2.1M tokens/wk)
- Latency SLOs for real-time flows (p95 < 250ms)
- Need predictable monthly spend for procurement and internal chargeback

How Redwood can help (high level)
- Batching + KV-prefix caching for session-based calls to reduce per-token compute by ~22–35% depending on session mix
- Quantization option for lower-throughput endpoints to save ~15–25% on GPU costs while preserving quality for classification tasks
- Dedicated capacity or reserved bursts to lock in predictable unit pricing and avoid egress surprises

Immediate asks you mentioned
1) A concise TCO sketch showing a 90-day pilot with expected token run-rate, projected savings from batching/caching, and a pilot quote for reserved capacity.
2) A short pilot scope (who, what, success metrics) and an Ops checklist we can hand to your infra team.
3) The security questionnaire you emailed and an initial E2E sso/keystore note for legal.

I attached a one-page TCO sketch (high-level numbers) and a starter pilot-scope workbook — both intentionally conservative. If this aligns, we can turn the sketch into a formal pilot quote for procurement.

Next steps (proposed)
- I’ll send a slightly-expanded TCO with two sensitivity scenarios (conservative / optimistic) by EOD tomorrow. [Attachment: FTX_tco_sketch.pdf]
- Marissa will produce a short pilot one-pager and a pilot ops checklist. [Attachment: pilot-scope.xlsx]
- Connor to loop in infra for a brief network/VM sizing sync if you want to evaluate a VPC/private deployment.

Can you confirm: 1) the primary approver at Fiscotech for a pilot (name + procurement email), and 2) the preferred start window (you mentioned late June)?

Appreciate the time — happy to hop on a quick follow-up with procurement if useful.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147
[Attachment: FTX_tco_sketch.pdf (pdf, 48KB)]

From: Clara Nguyen <clara@fiscotech.io>

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Affordability sizing & savings walkthrough — post-demo next steps

Thanks, Vivek — very useful framing. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming the approver: procurement is led by Mateo Alvarez (mateo.alvarez@fiscotech.io). I’ll intro you to him if you want procurement in the thread.
- Our target start window is indeed late June — ideally week of June 21. We have a month-long procurement window and need the pilot price and scope to review by the procurement kickoff (June 7).

Budget constraints: 
- Current carve-out for ML infra is $55k/month for the quarter; pilot funding needs to sit inside that or be justified vs. other pipeline projects.
- We can stretch to $80k/month if the ROI projection (savings + feature velocity) is clear.

Pilot success metrics:
- >=20% reduction in per-token cost for the classification pipeline;
- p95 latency <300ms across peak flows;
- no degradation in 5% random QA sample of classification outputs.

Can you include a short line item estimating one-off onboarding effort (hours + who does what)? Also please share your SOC2/Security questionnaire answers; procurement will expect that as part of the packet.

Happy to be looped to Mateo, and please send the detailed sensitivity scenarios tomorrow so we can prepare for procurement.

—Clara
Clara Nguyen
Head of Product | Fiscotech
clara@fiscotech.io
[Attachment: fiscotech-security-qs.pdf (pdf, 220KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Affordability sizing & savings walkthrough — post-demo next steps

Hi Clara / Mateo —

Thanks for the quick reply, Clara — Mateo, great to e-meet you. I’ve attached an updated TCO sketch with two sensitivity scenarios and a short onboarding estimate; I also included a one-line SOC2 status and the redwood contact for security evidence (we’ll share the questionnaire PDF in the next email to keep attachments tidy).

Highlights from the TCO sketch (conservative vs optimistic):
- Baseline token run-rate we modeled: 2.1M tokens/week (classification + summarization mix)
- Conservative: 20% expected compute savings from batching + KV caching -> ~USD 18k/mo savings; pilot cost (30-day reserved micro-pool + infra ops support) ~USD 42k
- Optimistic: 33% savings -> ~USD 30k/mo savings; pilot cost ~USD 48k with a 3% applied discount for early commitment
- One-off onboarding estimate: 40–60 engineer hours (Redwood + Fiscotech combined); split noted in attached workbook.

Pilot proposed scope (short)
- Duration: 30–45 days, target start: week of June 21
- Environments: staging + a single prod-like route for classification (sample traffic), limited traffic shaping to mimic peak flows
- Success metrics: those you listed (>=20% per-token cost reduction, p95 <300ms, QA tolerance)

Attachments included here: FTX_tco_sketch.pdf, pilot-scope.xlsx. I’ll send the completed security questionnaire and a short procurement-ready one-pager immediately after this note.

If that looks good I’ll put together a pilot SOW draft for procurement and Marissa will produce the one-pager for your procurement packet.

Cheers,
Vivek
